title: Dell's AI server backlog hits $132.3B as AI orders reach $60.2B
content:
ROUND ROCK, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)--
Dell Technologies (NYSE: DELL) announces financial results for its fiscal 2027 third quarter and provides guidance for its fiscal 2027 fourth quarter and full year.
Third-Quarter Summary
- Record revenue of $54.9 billion, up 103% year over year
- Record diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $8.82, up 287% year over year, and record non-GAAP diluted EPS of $9.45, up 265%
- Record third-quarter cash flow from operations of $4.5 billion
- Full-year FY27 revenue guidance of $202.0 billion, up 78% year over year
- Full-year FY27 diluted EPS guidance of $28.24 and non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance of $29.68, up 225% and 188% year over year, respectively
“We expect record full-year revenue of $202 billion, up 78%. We are now a different company, with Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) driving the vast majority of our profit and growth,” said Jeff Clarke, vice chairman and chief operating officer, Dell Technologies. “We ended the quarter with a record $132.3 billion AI backlog after booking $60.2 billion of orders, each rigorously vetted for customer quality and access to capital, land and power. Customers turn that backlog into revenue sooner because we test the complete rack before it ships and stand it up within six hours of delivery, which shortens time-to-first-token. Demand continues to accelerate and broaden globally, with more than 7,500 customers deploying Dell AI Factories.”
“The team executed exceptionally well, driving record revenue of $54.9 billion, record EPS and a record $4.9 billion returned to shareholders,” said David Kennedy, chief financial officer, Dell Technologies. “Operating expenses as a percentage of revenue continues to decline, while non-GAAP operating expenses fell to 7% of revenue, the lowest in our 42-year history. We’ve continued to run the company more efficiently as we’ve grown, and that is driving higher profitability, even as AI servers become a larger part of our business. We’ve generated record year-to-date cash flow from operations of $10.8 billion, and the Board approved a $25 billion increase to our repurchase authorization, reflecting confidence in long-term value creation.”
Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG)
- Record revenue: $42.0 billion, up 198% year over year
- Record AI-Optimized Servers revenue: $22.0 billion, up 291% year over year
- Record Traditional Servers and Networking revenue: $15.0 billion, up 235% year over year
- Record third-quarter Storage revenue: $4.9 billion, up 24% year over year
- Record operating income: $7.1 billion, up 308% year over year
Client Solutions Group (CSG)
- Revenue: $12.9 billion, up 3% year over year
- Operating income: $704 million, down 6% year over year
Capital Return
Dell Technologies returned a record $4.9 billion to shareholders in the third quarter through share repurchases and dividends.
The Company’s Board of Directors has also approved the repurchase of an additional $25.0 billion of shares of the Company’s Class C common stock under the stock repurchase program previously approved by the Board of Directors.

Conference call information
As previously announced, the company will hold a conference call to discuss its performance and financial guidance on Nov. 24 at 3:30 p.m. CST. Prior to the start of the conference call, prepared remarks and a presentation containing additional financial and operating information may be downloaded from investors.delltechnologies.com. The conference call will be presented live over the internet and can be accessed at https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-events/upcoming-events.
For those unable to listen to the live presentation, the final remarks and presentation with additional financial and operating information will be available following the presentation, and an archived version will be available at the same location for one year.
About Dell Technologies
Dell Technologies (NYSE: DELL) helps organizations and individuals build their digital future and transform how they work, live and play. The company provides customers with the industry’s broadest and most innovative technology and services portfolio for the AI era.

report.summary: Dell reports a record $132.3B AI server backlog after $60.2B in AI orders, driven by accelerating AI infrastructure demand.
report.background: Dell's results reflect the broader shift from general-purpose servers to GPU-heavy, rack-scale AI infrastructure. As enterprises move from AI pilots to production, demand has surged for complete AI factories—compute, networking, storage and deployment services—rather than individual servers. That demand is constrained by access to power, land and capital, so vendors are increasingly vetting orders for deliverability, not just collecting them. Dell, historically a PC-centric company, is repositioning around its Infrastructure Solutions Group, which now drives most profit and growth. The numbers also arrive amid intense competition among server makers and cloud providers, and as AI infrastructure spending reshapes IT budgets. Dell's ability to test and stand up full racks quickly is part of its pitch to shorten time-to-first-token for customers.
key_points: Dell booked $60.2 billion in AI orders in the quarter, pushing its AI server backlog to a record $132.3 billion. Management says orders are vetted for customer quality and access to capital, land and power—signals that demand is real but constrained by physical infrastructure, not just chip supply.

Infrastructure Solutions Group became the growth engine: revenue hit $42.0 billion, up 198%, while AI-optimized servers reached $22.0 billion, up 291%. ISG operating income rose 308% to $7.1 billion, showing AI servers are now driving Dell's profit, not just top-line growth.

Dell says it tests the complete rack before shipment and can stand it up within six hours of delivery, shortening time-to-first-token. More than 7,500 customers are deploying Dell AI Factories, indicating enterprise AI adoption is spreading beyond hyperscalers into broader global customers.

Total revenue reached $54.9 billion, up 103%, with record diluted EPS of $8.82 and non-GAAP EPS of $9.45. Operating expenses fell to 7% of revenue, the lowest in 42 years, and Dell guided FY27 revenue to $202 billion, up 78%, as AI servers scale.

Dell returned $4.9 billion to shareholders and boosted its buyback authorization by $25 billion. Meanwhile Client Solutions Group revenue was $12.9 billion, up only 3%, with operating income down 6%, highlighting how AI infrastructure now outpaces the traditional PC business.
report.impact: The backlog shows AI infrastructure spending remains intense and concentrated in a few server vendors and Nvidia-based systems. For the industry, it validates the 'AI factory' model but also spotlights constraints—power, land, capital—that will shape who can deploy. For developers, faster rack-level deployment and validated stacks could shorten time from hardware to inference, though access may still flow through cloud or large enterprises. For regular users, the benefits arrive indirectly through more capable AI services and potentially higher cloud costs as infrastructure demand strains supply. Dell's PC weakness also suggests AI spending is crowding out other IT budgets.
report.tools: To follow the stack, watch Dell AI Factory and NVIDIA HGX/DGX reference designs for enterprise deployments. For hands-on learning, try Kubernetes for orchestration, Kubeflow or Red Hat OpenShift AI for ML workflows, Ray for distributed compute, and vLLM for high-throughput inference. These open-source tools mirror parts of the rack-scale AI infrastructure Dell is selling.
